# E4h — what is actually slow inside `vlm_prefix`, kernel by kernel

**Generated by `bench/analyze_vlm_prefix.py` from the C1 ncu CSVs.** Nothing typed in.

C1 judged each phase by averaging its kernels weighted by duration. That is the right summary and the wrong resolution for deciding what to fix: a phase whose weighted average reads "latency bound" can be one large GEMM that is not, plus a tail of small kernels that are. A fix is applied to a kernel, so this asks the question per kernel.

**Read the shares as shares of the captured window.** `ncu -c 40` takes the first 40 kernels of the NVTX range, not a duration-weighted sample of the whole phase. The window is the start of the prefix and is representative of its kernel mix; a kernel that runs only late in the phase is not in it.
